summary.text: The translators' preface to the Persian edition notes that cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer in women worldwide, causing 266,000 deaths in 2012, and that although its reported prevalence in Iran is lower than in some countries its mortality risk is higher, making organized screening a necessity. It describes how the translation was undertaken with WHO permission, completed in four months with each part translated by two members, checked word by word and reviewed, and asks readers to email any errors they find.

summary.text: Describes, in the Persian translation, how evidence was synthesized: because randomized trials linking screen-and-treat strategies to health outcomes for all screened women are scarce, the recommendations rely on modelling from reviews of screening-test accuracy and of treatment effects. It details the searches of MEDLINE and EMBASE to February 2012, an update of a Cochrane review comparing HPV testing with cytology to November 2012 and a colposcopy search to September 2012, with independent screening by two reviewers and inclusion criteria such as low risk of bias, verification by a reference standard and non-pregnant women aged 18 or over not previously treated.

It explains how the HPV-test and HPV-test-then-VIA strategies decide who is treated and gives rescreening intervals of three to five years after negative VIA or cytology, at least five years after a negative HPV test, and follow-up one year after treatment.
